Size

iOS AR engine

Anchors to a horizontal plane and locks scale. If AR misbehaves on your device, switch to model-viewer to compare.

Android AR mode

Auto picks by device: the floor lock needs headroom an entry-level phone doesn't have, so weaker devices get Scene Viewer, which is a native app and much faster there.

Scene Viewer blending (occlusion)

Lets the rug pass under furniture — but on a phone with no depth sensor it costs frames and adds artefacts. Auto follows the device tier.

What the retailer actually integrates

    
One script tag and one function call. No model pipeline, no asset uploads, no per-SKU
      preparation — the rug photo already on their CDN is the only input. Everything below is live on this page.


    

      
12
triangles

        
A rug is a flat extruded outline. There is no mesh to optimise, so the model pipeline that a car needs simply doesn't exist here.

      
—
ms to build the AR model

        
Assembled in the browser, per view, from the retailer's own image bytes. Nothing is pre-baked.

      
0
image bytes through our servers

        
The photo is fetched straight from the retailer's CDN. We never store, process, or serve it — which is why marginal cost per view rounds to zero.

      
350k
SKUs supported on day one

        
Any SKU with a top-down photo and a size works immediately. Onboarding is not a per-SKU task.

    



<!-- once, in the site template -->
<script src="https://cdn.rugar.io/t/rugstudio/v1.js" async></script>

<!-- on the product page, whenever the shopper changes size or shape -->
RugAR.configure({
  sku:       "276826",
  name:      "Safavieh Aria ARA587P Rust / Blue",
  imageUrl:  "https://res.cloudinary.com/rugstudio-com/.../s_ara587p-5.jpg",
  width:     63,        // inches
  length:    91,
  shape:     "rectangle", // rectangle | square | round | runner | octagon
  thickness: 0.25       // inches — their own spec sheet
});


    

      
Try it with any rug in their catalogue

      
This is the claim worth testing live: no SKU was prepared in advance. Copy any product
         page address from rugstudio.com, paste it here, and it becomes an AR model. A direct
         image URL works too.

      

        
        
      

      
Their product pages send no CORS header, so the page is read
         server-side and the rug photo is pulled from the URL it points to.
